summary: Automated reports can create convincing but weakly grounded narratives, duplicate known work, and consume attention faster than teams can validate or act on findings.

points.text: A model may infer causality from correlated dashboards or quote stale ADRs as current policy. Aggregating more sources can increase narrative confidence without increasing correctness.
Frequent scheduled reports produce alert fatigue and repeated tickets unless findings have fingerprints, suppression rules, and a closed-loop disposition state.
Granting one job access to logs, roadmaps, incidents, and source code creates a concentrated privacy and secrets boundary; generated artifacts can leak data to broader audiences.
The report generator may optimize visible metrics and miss qualitative risks, local context, or work deliberately excluded from the indexed systems.
